_note: Reviewable suggestion register. Nothing here is implemented by default. Each row carries the evidence for it, what it would change, the risk, how to measure whether it worked, and the exact instruction block to feed into the next build prompt. 'expected_effect' values are hypotheses to test, never forecasts — do not present them as projected traffic or revenue. Status vocabulary: 'shipped' = implemented in an earlier session; 'done-this-session' = implemented by the session named in reviewed_by_session; 'recommended-now' / 'open' / 'open-blocked' = still to decide.

suggestions.title: Gate reader links until the Associates one-link test is done
suggestions.problem: Every buy button is built as amazon.com/dp/<observed ASIN>?tag=shopnow047c-20 from a fallback redirect target, and the tracking ID itself is unconfirmed (FLG-001, FLG-002). A monetised link whose tracking ID is not issued is worse than no link: it earns nothing and it is the classic reason accounts get closed.
suggestions.proposal: Ship the site with the buy buttons present but marked `data-link-state="pending-verification"` and a visible line on each product page: 'Destination and tracking not yet confirmed — we are testing one link per product before we scale.' Turn buttons into plain text only if the owner prefers zero risk.
suggestions.risk: Low. Temporarily suppresses the only monetisation path.
suggestions.expected_effect: Removes the highest-severity account risk before traffic exists. Measure: zero unconfirmed-tag links in the build; gate check passes.
suggestions.evidence: Amazon Associates Operating Agreement + Program Policies (S01, S02) as cited on the Verification page; both are login-gated, so confirm in your own console (FLG-006 note in sources).
suggestions.feeds_prompt: Run the one-link-per-product Associates test for the five observed ASINs, record destination + tracking-report confirmation per product, and only then remove data-link-state="pending-verification". Keep intended_* fields blank unless the owner confirms intent in writing.
suggestions.status_detail: Still the first thing to do: it gates every monetised link on the site.

suggestions.title: Publish the missing cluster half (thermometers had zero guides)
suggestions.problem: Two of five products sat in a cluster with no buying guide at all, while the About page asserted 'Meat Thermometers (2 products, 1 guide)'. A two-product category with no guide is a dead end: no internal links in, no reason to rank.
suggestions.proposal: Publish 'Instant-read or leave-in probe' and 'Cooking for a crowd this season', both anchored to USDA FSIS temperature guidance rather than to product adjectives. Compute the cluster counts in About from data so the claim can never drift again.
suggestions.risk: Low. Adds pages to index; no reader-trust exposure since no testing claims are made.
suggestions.expected_effect: Category no longer orphaned; thermometer pages gain internal links. Measure: Search Console impressions/clicks for thermometer queries after 4 weeks.
suggestions.evidence: File-level inspection: guides/ contained 4 files, none in the thermometer cluster; about_body() hardcoded the wrong count.
suggestions.feeds_prompt: Keep cluster counts computed from data/guides/*.json and data/products.json — never hand-written — and add a gate check that fails if any category has zero guides.
suggestions.status_detail: Shipped by session arena-23d7ed19 on 2026-11-20.

suggestions.title: Replace emoji thumbnails with real imagery
suggestions.problem: The only 'imagery' on the site was a 🍟 and a 🌡️ glyph in each card, and there was no og:image at all, so a shared link rendered as a blank grey card. This is the single clearest 'generated, not published' tell.
suggestions.proposal: Add commissioned editorial illustrations (kitchen counter, air-fryer baskets, probes, holiday scene) with honest captions stating they are illustrations, plus og:image + twitter:card per page. Never scrape Amazon product images: the IP License restricts their use.
suggestions.risk: Low, with one rule: every image must be labelled as an illustration and must never be captioned as the product a reader will receive.
suggestions.expected_effect: Higher click-through from social/messaging shares; warmer read. Measure: outbound_click per session on illustrated vs pre-change pages, and share-click rate once the endpoint exists.
suggestions.evidence: assets/ contained no image files (verified by directory listing); head() emitted no og:image.
suggestions.feeds_prompt: Commission licensed lifestyle photography for the five products and both categories; keep the 'no Amazon product images' rule, keep the illustration captions, and swap files in without touching copy. Never scrape Amazon imagery.
suggestions.status_detail: Illustrations shipped; the licensed-photography decision (Q-07) is still open.

suggestions.title: Fix the navigation so labels match destinations
suggestions.problem: The 'Guides' item pointed at one specific guide and 'Products' pointed at one specific product page. Both labels were promises the link did not keep, and no index page existed for either. Eight flat nav items also mixed reader pages with internal dashboard pages.
suggestions.proposal: Create guides/index.html and products/index.html, point the nav at them, and collapse the five operations pages into one 'The Desk' group (footer keeps every surface reachable, per the brief).
suggestions.risk: None. New index pages must be added to the sitemap — the build generates it, so this is automatic.
suggestions.expected_effect: Fewer dead ends, more pages per session. Measure: pages/session and the share of sessions that reach a second product page.
suggestions.evidence: Rendered nav HTML in index.html: href="guides/basket-or-oven-style-air-fryer.html" labelled 'Guides'; no guides/index.html existed on disk.
suggestions.feeds_prompt: Keep nav generated from one NAV list in the builder and assert in the gate that every nav label resolves to an index page, not a leaf.
suggestions.status_detail: Shipped by session arena-23d7ed19 on 2026-11-20.

suggestions.title: Stop showing unrelated products inside a guide
suggestions.problem: guide_body() rendered all five products into every guide's 'Shop the comparison' block, so the basket-vs-oven air fryer guide ended with two meat thermometers. Readers notice. It also diluted the internal-link logic that makes a cluster rank.
suggestions.proposal: Filter the CARDS block by each guide's category field, with an explicit cross-sell line when a related cluster genuinely helps ('if you are roasting, see the probe guides'). One guide already does this by hand; make the builder do it for all of them.
suggestions.risk: Low. Needs a fallback for guides with no matching products so the section never renders empty.
suggestions.expected_effect: More relevant internal links. Measure: outbound_click rate per guide before/after, once SG-01 lifts.
suggestions.evidence: scripts/build_site.py guide_body(): product_card(p, depth=1) for p in PRODUCTS — unfiltered.
suggestions.feeds_prompt: Change guide CARDS to filter by the guide's category field and add a gate check that fails if a guide's product block contains a product from another category.
suggestions.status_detail: Shipped by session arena-23d7ed19 on 2026-11-20: guide CARDS are filtered by the guide's category field with a fallback. This register still said 'open' until this session's audit — a register that misstates its own status is worse than no register.

suggestions.title: Move content out of the builder into files
suggestions.problem: All four guides lived as Python string literals inside an 841-line builder. Adding a guide meant editing code, which is how cadence dies — and it is how a stray quote takes down a deploy.
suggestions.proposal: Load guides from data/guides/*.json (verbatim migration, no copy edits), sort by published date, and add scripts/new_guide.py so a new guide is 'drop a file, run build'. Sitemap, RSS, search index and cluster counts all pick it up from the same source.
suggestions.risk: Medium — touched the build path, so it must stay gated: `npm run build && npm run check` green before merge.
suggestions.expected_effect: One-command cadence. Measure: time from 'topic chosen' to 'page live'; number of builder edits needed to publish (target: zero).
suggestions.evidence: GUIDES list at scripts/build_site.py:298-446; three separate loops iterated it.
suggestions.feeds_prompt: Keep data/guides/*.json as the only guide source; extend scripts/new_guide.py with --cluster and --season flags and a pre-fill that refuses to write a guide with no source link per table row.
suggestions.status_detail: Shipped by session arena-23d7ed19 on 2026-11-20.

suggestions.title: Deploy the metrics endpoint before writing anything else
suggestions.problem: The five events, the client beacon and the worker code all exist, and CONFIG.endpoint is an empty string, so nothing is counted anywhere except in the visitor's own browser. The brief's priority — measure before you optimise — is currently unmet by one deployment step.
suggestions.proposal: Deploy analytics/worker.js (Cloudflare Worker or a 20-line Flask app behind any host you already own), set CONFIG.endpoint, and keep the campaign ledger empty until first-party reports arrive. No IP stored, no cookies, no fingerprinting — the code already behaves that way; keep it that way at deploy time.
suggestions.cost: ≈0 at this traffic (worker free tier / existing host)
suggestions.risk: Privacy exposure if you later add IP logging; write the retention rule down before you deploy, not after.
suggestions.expected_effect: Real denominators for every future decision. Measure: events/day > 0 and ledger rows timestamped from the endpoint, not from guesses.
suggestions.evidence: assets/app.js CONFIG.endpoint === "" (local-only mode); FLG-007 states the endpoint is shipped, not deployed.
suggestions.feeds_prompt: Deploy analytics/worker.js, set CONFIG.endpoint in assets/app.js, confirm all five events land, and add a nightly count to the campaign ledger table. Do not fabricate backfill for the days before go-live.
suggestions.status_detail: Still open: the endpoint code exists but is not deployed, so no event leaves a browser.

suggestions.title: Verify Search Console ownership and let queries pick topic six
suggestions.problem: Nothing tells us which questions people actually arrive with. The four original guide titles were hypotheses from the brief, explicitly labelled as such; a fifth and sixth topic chosen the same way is just more guessing.
suggestions.proposal: Add the domain to Search Console, submit sitemap.xml, wait for ~4 weeks of query data, then choose the next two guides from real impressions where we rank 8-25 (the band where one good page moves you).
suggestions.risk: None beyond a few weeks of patience.
suggestions.expected_effect: Topics chosen from demand instead of taste. Measure: query list saved into data/queries-log.json with a dated provenance line, as the campaign ledger does for clicks.
suggestions.evidence: The brief's Priority 4 ('the next topic is chosen from measured queries instead of instinct'); no SC property exists yet (FLG-007 adjacent).
suggestions.feeds_prompt: After Search Console has 4 weeks of data, export queries where the site ranks 8-25 with >50 impressions, store them in data/queries-log.json with the export date, and generate one guide per chosen query from the data/guides/_template.json file.
suggestions.status_detail: Still open: no Search Console property exists, so no topic on the backlog is chosen from measured queries yet.

suggestions.title: Get a real byline, or say plainly that there isn't one
suggestions.problem: Every page is bylined 'the ShopNow Kitchen Desk'. The site is honest about it — About says it does not invent credentials or hands-on reviews, which is the correct behaviour. But search quality raters and readers both weight identifiable humans, and a desk byline with no addressable person caps how far this can go.
suggestions.proposal: Owner supplies one real name, one short bio with actual experience, and a contact route. Until then, keep the desk byline and keep the 'we do not test' disclosure exactly where it is. Do not fabricate a person: a fake named expert is a material misrepresentation, not a style choice.
suggestions.cost: none — but it is a decision only the owner can make
suggestions.risk: Publishing a real name attaches the compliance exposure to a person. Choose deliberately.
suggestions.expected_effect: E-E-A-T signal, reviewer identity for later product-schema work. Measure: nothing automated; re-check after 3 months.
suggestions.evidence: about_body() authorship copy; brief's 'authorship' requirement in the publication pass.
suggestions.feeds_prompt: Add data/authors.json with {name, bio, credentials, contact, orcid_or_links}, render bylines from it, and keep the current 'no hands-on testing' disclosure line intact wherever a byline appears.
suggestions.status_detail: Still open: the desk byline is honest but caps trust signals.

suggestions.title: Resolve the two live spec conflicts before anyone cites this page
suggestions.problem: B08DKYBTPH carries contradictory model and max-temperature strings, and today's re-observation reproduced the same conflict: that listing's own <title> reads 'TurboFry 4-in-1 ... 450°F Hi-Fry' while the recorded title string says 'TurboFry Touch ... Family Size' with 200-400°F. Separately, the Emeril page says 'six accessories' in the title and '7 Accessories' in the bullets, and the ThermoMaven ASIN variant (B0DMDQZTZN) is still unresolved (FLG-004, FLG-005, FLG-010).
suggestions.proposal: Re-read the live listing, prefer the manufacturer product page over Amazon marketing copy for numeric specs, and record the chosen source per cell. Where two official sources disagree, show both with their dates instead of silently picking one.
suggestions.risk: Low, but do not 'fix' it by averaging or guessing — a wrong number here is the kind of error that gets quoted for years.
suggestions.expected_effect: The pages become citable. Measure: zero cells flagged 'conflicts' in the specs table.
suggestions.evidence: data/products.json p3/p4/p2 fields; data/probes.json notes from the 2026-11-20 re-observation.
suggestions.feeds_prompt: For each conflicted spec cell, fetch the manufacturer's own page, record URL + retrieval date in data/sources.json, and render both values with dates when sources disagree instead of choosing one.
suggestions.status_detail: Partly closed: the third read on 2026-11-20 confirmed both conflicting strings on the live listing; the manufacturer page is still the only way to settle them.

suggestions.title: Add the two page types that convert, once links are verified
suggestions.problem: A product page and a category page are the two formats that actually earn clicks, and both currently stop at specs. There is no 'who should buy which' summary on the category page and no decision shortcut on product pages, because we cannot claim a preference without a method.
suggestions.proposal: Add a 'Match to your situation' block on each category page (three reader profiles, three answers, each answer traced to a listed spec), and a 'Before you buy on this page' checklist on product pages. Still no 'best' ranking: state the spec each answer rests on.
suggestions.risk: Medium for trust: any recommendation needs its reasoning visible, or it reads like the affiliate spam this site is positioned against.
suggestions.expected_effect: Higher outbound click rate with no claim inflation. Measure: outbound_click / page_view per category page.
suggestions.evidence: category_body() renders intro + guide links + cards, no decision block; brief's 'make it read like a shop'.
suggestions.feeds_prompt: Add a 'Match to your situation' module to category_body() driven by a per-category profiles list in data/categories.json, and require every rendered recommendation to name the spec it rests on (enforce in check_site.py).
suggestions.status_detail: Shipped by session arena-82d39deb on 2026-11-20: data/categories.json adds reader profiles per category, and each category page now renders a 'Match to your situation' block where every answer names the one listed spec it rests on. The photography half of this suggestion (licensed lifestyle shots) stays open under SG-03 / Q-07.

suggestions.title: Keep the compliance gate as the thing that cannot be skipped
suggestions.problem: The gate already checks disclosure strip, sponsored rel, tag presence, no prices, no link.amazon reader links, internal links and sitemap coverage — that is genuinely good. It does not check the claims that are easiest to get wrong by accident: a page asserting cluster counts, a guide with no source link, an image referenced but missing, a byline claiming testing.
suggestions.proposal: Extend check_site.py: every rendered count must be computed not typed; every guide table needs a source anchor; every must exist; a banned-phrase list for 'we tested', 'we tried', 'our lab', 'best overall'; a banned 'double opt-in' style promise when no code implements it. Keep the gate failing closed.
suggestions.risk: None. If it is too strict, loosen a rule deliberately rather than deleting the check.
suggestions.expected_effect: Truthfulness stops depending on the person editing. Measure: gate run on every commit; count of violations caught pre-merge.
suggestions.evidence: scripts/check_site.py inspected line by line (133 lines); banned-phrase and image-existence checks absent.
suggestions.feeds_prompt: Keep scripts/check_site.py failing closed; add the banned-phrase, computed-counts, image-exists and per-row-source checks, and never mark a task verified without an official source link in data/sources.json.
suggestions.status_detail: Shipped by session arena-23d7ed19 on 2026-11-20; extended again in this session (register-schema checks).

suggestions.title: Say what the capture form does — accurately
suggestions.problem: The newsletter block promises 'Double opt-in' and 'No tracking pixel'. The form records a local event and hands the address to whatever provider the owner later wires up; no double opt-in flow exists in this repo. A privacy promise the code does not keep is worse than a weaker promise that it does.
suggestions.proposal: Rewrite to match the implementation: what happens now, what is stored where, and that nothing leaves the device until an endpoint and a provider are configured. Then keep the copy and the code in the same pull request forever.
suggestions.risk: Low.
suggestions.expected_effect: Removes a false-claim surface (the exact category FTC guidance targets). Measure: banned-promise list in the gate.
suggestions.evidence: assets/app.js reader-capture handler records an event locally; capture_block() text in scripts/build_site.py.
suggestions.feeds_prompt: Rewrite capture copy to describe implemented behaviour only, and add 'Double opt-in' plus any other unimplemented privacy promise to the check_site.py banned list.
suggestions.status_detail: Shipped by session arena-23d7ed19 on 2026-11-20: the capture copy was rewritten to describe implemented behaviour only, and check_site.py now fails on unimplemented privacy promises. The 'double opt-in' phrase is on the gate's banned list.

suggestions.title: Let the robots file and the index say which files are not content
suggestions.problem: GitHub Pages serves the whole repo, and robots.txt said only 'Allow: /'. That leaves /scripts/, /data/, /analytics/ and the archived prior session's pages crawlable next to the real content — crawl budget spent on internals, and an unfinished feel.
suggestions.proposal: Disallow the implementation paths, keep the content paths open, keep the single sitemap reference. The archive stays on disk as provenance; it just is not offered to a crawler.
suggestions.risk: None — the archived pages are not in the sitemap either.
suggestions.expected_effect: Cleaner crawl set. Measure: indexed-page count in Search Console equals sitemap URL count.
suggestions.evidence: robots.txt before this session: three lines, no Disallow.
suggestions.feeds_prompt: Keep robots.txt generated by the builder so the Disallow list cannot drift from the repo layout, and re-check after adding any new top-level directory.
suggestions.status_detail: Shipped by session arena-23d7ed19 on 2026-11-20.

suggestions.title: Front page should sell the shop, not describe the process
suggestions.status_detail: Shipped in this session. The front page no longer counts its own sources and flags; the audit furniture moved to the Desk.
suggestions.problem: The front page led with 'Why the numbers here are boring in a good way' — four bullets counting sources, flags and open questions — and the newsletter block explained its own broken implementation in reader copy ('records a count inside your own browser'). The brief asks for a publication front page that leads with the products, with every dashboard surface reachable from the footer and one navigation group. A visitor who arrived from a search was asked to read about our bookkeeping before seeing anything to buy.
suggestions.proposal: Rebuild the front page in the order a reader moves: hero (one question), the shop (cards with specs and a sponsored button), the guides that answer that question, the two categories, then one short honest line about how the site works with a link to the full method. Move the counts, the flags and the questions to the Desk pages, where they belong.
suggestions.risk: Low. The information is not deleted, it is moved to pages that are still one click from every page.
suggestions.expected_effect: A reader reaches a product or a guide before meeting the process. Measure: outbound_click rate on the front page once the endpoint exists (SG-07).
suggestions.evidence: Rendered index.html on 2026-11-20 (before this session): the section 'Why the numbers here are boring in a good way' and the capture block's self-describing caveat.
suggestions.feeds_prompt: Keep the front page in publication order — hero, shop, guides, categories, one-line method note — and never let a count of sources, flags or questions appear in the reader path. Dashboard surfaces live in the footer and the single 'The Desk' navigation group.

suggestions.title: Every category needs a decision shortcut that names its deciding spec
suggestions.status_detail: Shipped in this session: data/categories.json + 'Match to your situation' block on both category pages.
suggestions.problem: A reader could read every spec on a category page and still not know which spec decides their case. The previous session flagged this as SG-11 and left it open because a recommendation without a stated method reads like affiliate spam.
suggestions.proposal: For each category, write reader situations ('two of you, most weeknights'), name the one listed spec that decides that situation, state what the listings actually say about it, and give the answer with the listing linked. Never rank; always name the spec the answer rests on.
suggestions.risk: Medium for trust: a profile that reaches beyond the listed specs becomes an opinion. The compliance gate checks that every profile names a field that exists in data/products.json.
suggestions.expected_effect: Faster decisions and more outbound clicks without inflating any claim. Measure: outbound_click per category page once SG-07 is deployed.
suggestions.evidence: category_body() before this session rendered intro + cards + a comparison table + guide links, and nothing that answered 'which one for me'.
suggestions.feeds_prompt: Keep profiles in data/categories.json, one deciding spec per profile, and extend the gate so a profile that names a field absent from data/products.json fails the build.

suggestions.title: Publish the question backlog so the pipeline is visible
suggestions.status_detail: Shipped in this session: data/topics.json renders as topics.html, linked from the guides index, the front page and the sitemap.
suggestions.problem: The brief asks to publish question-shaped guides and then measure whether anyone arrives. Nothing on the site recorded what was planned, what was published, or how each topic was chosen — so the cadence was invisible and the 'why this topic' question had no public answer.
suggestions.proposal: Add a topics page listing planned guides with the reader question, the sources each would need, and a 'chosen from' line that says plainly whether the topic came from an editorial hypothesis or from a measured query. Keep published guides separate from planned ones.
suggestions.risk: Low, but the honesty matters: a page of planned topics must not read like a demand forecast.
suggestions.expected_effect: A visible editorial pipeline, and a place where a measured query can replace a hypothesis once Search Console data exists. Measure: number of topics whose 'chosen from' changes from hypothesis to measured query.
suggestions.evidence: No page in the 2026-11-20 build listed planned topics; the only trace of the backlog was in the COORDINATION.md session log.
suggestions.feeds_prompt: Keep the backlog in data/topics.json, mark every planned topic's chosen_from explicitly, and never label a topic 'popular' or 'trending' without measured query data.

suggestions.title: Read a spec row from the product's own details table, never from a sibling product
suggestions.status_detail: Shipped in this session: the third independent re-read found one wrong row (the 8-quart Chefman's wattage) and it was corrected with the prior capture kept.
suggestions.problem: The 8-quart Chefman was recorded at 1700W / 120V, which is the wattage printed on the 6-quart Chefman listing. The live bullet for the 8-quart reads '1000 Watts/120 Volts – RJ38-SQSS-8T'. A reader comparing power draw would have been reading a number copied from a different product.
suggestions.proposal: Make the details-table read mandatory for any spec row, keep the prior capture beside the corrected value so the change is visible, and re-read the remaining rows (model, UPC, weight) for the two thermometers, whose model and package details are still partly blank or inferred from another marketplace.
suggestions.risk: Low. The rule protects against the single most likely silent error: a plausible number from the wrong source.
suggestions.expected_effect: Spec rows stop drifting from their source. Measure: number of corrected values per verification pass — target zero after this pass.
suggestions.evidence: data/products.json p3-chefman-8qt: power was '1700W / 120V' until the 2026-11-20 third read; now '1000W / 120V' with power_prior_capture kept (FLG-022).
suggestions.feeds_prompt: Re-read a product's own details table and bullet copy before recording any spec row, keep the previous value as *_prior_capture, and open a flag whenever two official sources disagree instead of choosing one.

suggestions.title: Decide the imagery line: licensed photography or the illustration set
suggestions.status_detail: Still open. Illustrations are shipped and honestly captioned; this is the decision about replacing them with real product photography.
suggestions.problem: The current illustrations are honest and consistent, but a buyer's first question about an affiliate page is 'what does it actually look like'. Illustrations answer the mood, not the product. Amazon's IP licence restricts the use of Amazon-hosted product imagery, so the answer is licensed photography, a shoot, or nothing.
suggestions.proposal: Either commission a small set of licensed lifestyle shots for the five products and two categories (and replace the illustration captions with real credits), or decide to stay with the illustration line and say so on the About page as a standing editorial rule. Do not scrape Amazon images.
suggestions.cost: cash for licensed photography; zero for staying with illustrations
suggestions.risk: Cash and time if commissioned; a credibility gap if scraped imagery appears without rights.
suggestions.expected_effect: Better trust and click-through if photography ships; nothing measurable if the decision is to stay with illustrations. Measure: outbound_click per product page, once the endpoint exists.
suggestions.evidence: assets/img/ holds four original illustrations; About → Methodology states the no-Amazon-imagery rule; Q-07 asks where the images come from permanently.
suggestions.feeds_prompt: Decide the imagery line once, in writing, and either commission licensed photography with credits or record 'illustrations by policy' as the standing rule. Never use Amazon-hosted product images.

suggestions.title: Decide the audience and the marketplace before more content is written
suggestions.status_detail: Still open. It is the decision the content plan depends on most, and it costs nothing to decide.
suggestions.problem: Every page is English content pointing at amazon.com with a US-shaped tracking suffix, while the owner's locale is South Holland. There is no OneLink, no second marketplace enrolment and no translated content. Writing a year of guides before settling this risks a year of guides for the wrong reader.
suggestions.proposal: Answer Q-10 and Q-17 explicitly: which readers, which marketplace, which language. If US-only is the answer, say so on the About page and keep the tracking ID as-is. If EU readers matter, check per-marketplace Associates enrolment before the next content batch, because the product set and the legal requirements differ.
suggestions.cost: none to decide; a re-platforming cost if the answer changes
suggestions.risk: Deciding late is the expensive option: content written for the wrong market is sunk cost.
suggestions.expected_effect: One decision that unblocks topic choice, link format, and the imprint question. Measure: nothing to measure — this is a decision, not an experiment.
suggestions.evidence: FLG-011 (locale unresolved), Q-10 (audience), and the fact that all five links resolve to amazon.com listings while the owner operates in NL.
suggestions.feeds_prompt: Record the audience, marketplace and language decision in data/questions.json answers and on the About page, then re-check every outbound link format against that decision.

suggestions.title: Stop pasting the raw listing title into product cards
suggestions.problem: Every card on the front page, the shop index and the category pages rendered Amazon's keyword-stuffed listing title as its body copy — three near-identical paragraphs of 'Sync Finish, Hi-Fry, Auto Shutoff, Digital Double Air Fryer - Black'. That is the single loudest 'scraped affiliate template' tell on the site, and a buyer reads it as a bot.
suggestions.proposal: Write a short editorial card line per product, composed only from that product's own verified listing fields, and move the verbatim listing title to the product page where it belongs — as a quoted source, not as prose.
suggestions.risk: Low. The card must never add a fact the listing does not state; the gate now fails an empty or absent card_copy, so the line cannot silently rot into marketing copy.
suggestions.expected_effect: Cards read like a shop. Measure: card_copy present on 5/5 products, verbatim title still on every product page, gate green.
suggestions.evidence: data/products.json card_copy fields (each drawn from the fields sourced in S24, S25, S26, S28, S29, S30); the previous rendering is in git history for ba0b838.
suggestions.feeds_prompt: Keep reader card copy in data/products.json `card_copy`, written only from fields the register already sources. The verbatim Amazon listing title stays on the product page as a quoted source line, never as card prose.

suggestions.title: One illustration per product, not one per category
suggestions.problem: The three air-fryer cards shared one image and both thermometer cards shared another, so the shop grid looked like a mail-merge. Stock or Amazon product photography was not an option (licensing), which left commissioned illustration.
suggestions.proposal: Commission one flat editorial illustration per product and per new guide, captioned every time as an illustration that does not show the exact unit, and use it as the product page's og:image so a shared link is not a blank card.
suggestions.risk: Medium if a caption ever implies the picture is the product. The caption text is fixed in data and the gate checks the file exists.
suggestions.expected_effect: A shop that looks made rather than generated; share cards with art. Measure: 5/5 products with their own image, 0 images reused across product cards.
suggestions.evidence: assets/img/p-*.png (commissioned 2026-11-20); captions in data/products.json `card_image_caption`; Amazon Associates policy forbids copying listing imagery (S01, S02).
suggestions.feeds_prompt: Every product keeps its own `card_image` + `card_image_caption` in data/products.json, always captioned as an illustration, never as a photograph of the item. Reuse of one image across two product cards should fail the gate.

suggestions.title: Put a comparison the reader can finish on the front page
suggestions.problem: The at-a-glance comparison lived one click away on the shop index. A reader deciding between a two-basket fryer and an oven-style unit had to open two tabs, and most will not.
suggestions.proposal: Render a compact front-page table — what it is, the one spec that decides it, what to check at home — with a source link per row, built from the same data as the cards so it cannot drift.
suggestions.risk: Low. It is generated from data/products.json, so it updates with the register rather than against it.
suggestions.expected_effect: One-screen comparison on the landing page; outbound clicks from the front page become measurable via the existing event. Measure: front-page outbound_click events per session once the endpoint is deployed.
suggestions.evidence: data/products.json (all rows), S24/S25/S26/S28; measurement events defined in data/campaign-ledger.json + analytics/README.md.
suggestions.feeds_prompt: Keep the front-page at-a-glance table generated from data/products.json — one column per product, the deciding spec named, no prices, no ranking.

suggestions.title: Publish a seasonal front for the Thanksgiving cook — without price claims
suggestions.problem: The brief asks for topics that bring organic traffic. The season that actually moves kitchen-gear traffic is the one happening this week, and the site was displaying 'Season: Everyday' chips with nothing behind them.
suggestions.proposal: Publish the two holiday-probe guides, add a dated seasonal strip to the front page that links them, and keep every food-safety number sourced to USDA FSIS. No discount, price or availability claim anywhere, because those cannot be shown (S02).
suggestions.risk: Medium: a dated strip goes stale. It carries the date in its own text and the guide titles are question-shaped, so they stay useful after the week ends.
suggestions.expected_effect: Timely, genuinely useful pages that can rank for questions rather than brands. Measure: Search Console queries for the new guides after Q-13 is done.
suggestions.evidence: S16/S17 (USDA FSIS, read 2026-11-20), S29/S30 (the two thermometer listings re-read the same day).
suggestions.feeds_prompt: Seasonal surfaces must carry their date, cite USDA FSIS for any temperature, and never reference a price or discount (Program Policies S02; FLG-027).

suggestions.title: Clear three rows off the topic backlog instead of admiring it
suggestions.problem: topics.html listed thirteen questions and published none of them; the backlog was decoration. Three of those rows needed only data already in this repo.
suggestions.proposal: Write the accuracy-check, probe-placement and counter-fit guides from the existing sources, set their topics to `published` with a link back, and leave the honest rows planned.
suggestions.risk: Low. The gate refuses a published topic without a built page, so a status cannot be claimed without the file.
suggestions.expected_effect: Nine guides, three topics closed, and a backlog that shrinks. Measure: guides count on about.html (computed), impressions per guide page after Search Console.
suggestions.evidence: data/topics.json TP-06/TP-08/TP-09 flipped to published with published_as; data/guides/ three new files; S17 for every temperature claim.
suggestions.feeds_prompt: A topic moves to `published` only in the same commit as its guide file, and the gate checks the built page exists.

suggestions.title: Keep the bookkeeping out of the reader's sight, one click closer instead
suggestions.problem: Reader-facing card copy carried internal register ids ('— see FLG-005') inside a spec line, and the capture block explained its own missing backend. Both are audit language on a shop page.
suggestions.proposal: Strip ids from cards and product blurb copy, keep the full note on the product page where the flag belongs, and rewrite the sign-up block as one honest sentence that links to the disclosure and questions pages.
suggestions.risk: Low, if the gate enforces it — otherwise ids creep back. It now does: 'FLG-' inside a product card fails the build.
suggestions.expected_effect: Pages read like an editor wrote them; the audit trail stays one click away, not inline. Measure: zero flag ids in cards or index.html product grid.
suggestions.evidence: scripts/check_site.py reader-copy rules; index.html and product cards before/after in git history.
suggestions.feeds_prompt: Flag ids and register language never appear inside a product card or a reader blurb; they live on the product page, verification page and Flagged for Review page.

suggestions.title: Decide the price question now, not in December
suggestions.problem: The listings carry prices, ratings and deal badges; the site may not copy them and cannot refresh them, so in the highest-intent week of the year the only product instruction is 'check on Amazon'. That is compliant, and it is a conversion ceiling.
suggestions.proposal: Two ways out, pick one: (a) wire the Creator/PA API into a build step that writes prices with a fetch timestamp and the freshness note, or (b) formally adopt a no-price editorial stance and lean entirely on question-shaped guides. Today the site silently does (b) while pretending it is only a caution.
suggestions.cost: (a) needs API approval on the account; (b) costs nothing
suggestions.risk: (a) is the only compliant path to price display and it adds a stale-data risk each time the build is not re-run; (b) caps seasonal conversion. Doing neither leaves the ambiguity in the reader's face.
suggestions.expected_effect: Either prices appear with a date and a source, or the site states plainly that it compares features and never prices. Measure: outbound-click rate on seasonal pages, before and after.
suggestions.evidence: Program Policies price rule (S02, read 2026-11-20); deal badges and prices visible on the listings during the same read and not copied (FLG-027, S28).
suggestions.feeds_prompt: Record the chosen price stance on this register, then make the disclosure page, the product pages and the seasonal strip say the same thing; if (a) is chosen, prices come only from an API response stored with a timestamp.

suggestions.title: Pin or stop: either bind each link to a verified variant or say nothing about variants
suggestions.problem: A fourth observation of all five tokens again resolved to the same ASINs, but two responses now carried a variant parameter (th=1) and Amazon's own rails showed sibling listings — same product name, different colour or bundle. A reader can be served a listing this site does not describe.
suggestions.proposal: During the one-link Associates test (FLG-002), record the final URL with every query parameter per product; if the served variant differs, either link the variant explicitly or keep the bare /dp/<ASIN> form and remove any colour/bundle wording from product copy.
suggestions.risk: Low. The alternative — silent mismatch between the page and the landing listing — is the kind of thing that reads as bait and costs an account.
suggestions.expected_effect: What the page describes is what the link serves. Measure: five recorded final URLs with variant params in data/probes.json, and no variant claim that is not in that list.
suggestions.evidence: data/probes.json fourth_observation (2026-11-20), S28/S29/S30, FLG-026.
suggestions.feeds_prompt: Product copy may mention a colour, bundle or size only if that variant is recorded in the redirect log for the link the button uses.

suggestions.title: Write the two guides that only a measurement can justify — after the measurement
suggestions.problem: The remaining backlog rows that would need demand data ('how loud is an air fryer', 'fryer or thermometer first') cannot be written honestly from listings: one needs sound measurements nobody took, the other is a ranking we refuse to publish without a method.
suggestions.proposal: Hold those rows until the analytics endpoint and a Search Console property exist (Q-07/SG-08), then let queries in the 8–25 position choose the next two topics; the gate already refuses a topic that claims measured demand without a recorded source.
suggestions.cost: endpoint hosting (free tier) + one-time Search Console verification
suggestions.risk: If nothing is measured, the backlog keeps growing into decoration again; if the cadence is committed in Q-24, the hold has an end date.
suggestions.expected_effect: Topics chosen by evidence instead of instinct. Measure: two new guides whose `chosen_from` says 'measured query' with a date and the property that reported it.
suggestions.evidence: data/topics.json chosen_from provenance rule enforced in scripts/check_site.py; analytics/README.md for the endpoint; Q-13 in the questions register.
suggestions.feeds_prompt: Deploy analytics and verify Search Console, then pick the next two topics from recorded queries and set their chosen_from to 'measured query' with the date and the report path.

suggestions.title: Make the holiday guides usable on paper
suggestions.problem: The seasonal guides are read in a kitchen, often while hands are busy; right now they are screen-only prose with a table, and print output is unstyled except for hiding the nav.
suggestions.proposal: Add a print stylesheet for guides (source links as footnote references, disclosure kept), plus a one-line 'print this' note on the two holiday pages; no new facts, same sources.
suggestions.risk: Low. A printed page still has to carry the disclosure, which is why the print rule must keep the disclosure and drop only the navigation.
suggestions.expected_effect: A guide that survives being used. Measure: qualitative — one owner check of the printed preview — and no gate regression on disclosure.
suggestions.evidence: @media print rule in assets/style.css today hides nav, desk group, capture and disclosure strip; FTC guidance on clear and conspicuous disclosure (S03).
suggestions.feeds_prompt: Guides get a print stylesheet that keeps the disclosure sentence and renders source links as numbered footnotes.
